summary: Gradient-boosted trees on residue and (q/p) features predict the least-C class (C=1, 2, ≥3) at 81.7% CV vs a 73.1% majority baseline; the top features are the p mod 3, 5, 7, 11 indicators and (41/p). The predictability is the known small-modulus residue structure, with no non-residue predictor found.

Web check: search hits identify ES with Erdős Problem 242 (a GitHub issue titled 'Erdős Problem 242: Erdős–Straus Proof' appears, unverified, and erdosproblems.com was not visited directly). No reusable unit-fraction Lean lemma library was identified for ES in this check.

Greedy template covers per class mod 840 (r = 1, 121, 169, 289, 361, 529; templates (C,d), C ≤ 200, d | 4Cp+1, d ≡ −1 mod 4C) at X = 10^5 (40–50 primes per class) need 21–27 templates, about one template per two primes, with no uncovered primes. The communication cost grows with the number of primes in the class, so there is no bounded per-class dictionary at this range; the global dictionary is small (Z1788).

The query count for worst-case C is the C_min distribution: records 1,2,5,20,...,557, 23105 at p=184837; 99% quantile 9 (fingerprint #180, #183). Adaptive vs fixed order was not improved by any test here.

Character-sparse fits of f(p) are the fingerprint character-weight lane: dominant characters are the quadratic (q/p) for small q, with the q mod 3 dichotomy of the weights (fingerprint #152; H00 Z0199).

Max C_min over p is already tracked: the record sequence keeps growing (23105 at p=184837, a boundary solution; fingerprint #180). The 'unbounded C_min' question is an empirical record sequence, not a provable statement, and nothing new was computed.

Lookup (web search): the unit-fraction Lean/Xena formalisation exists, and Erdős #306 has a 2026 elementary proof. None of these supplies a lemma library for 4/n certificates; finite n-ranges are already certified by computer search, so a Lean checker adds verification, not mathematics.

Chain rule C' = C(q+1) (for q | 4Cp+1 with q ∤ 4C, q | 4C'p+1 holds) on 400 primes in (10^3, 10^5]: the linear C-scan succeeds at median C = 1 and p90 C = 3, and the chain fails within 40 steps for 87/400 primes because C grows multiplicatively. The chain gives no advantage.
k-means (k = 4) on residue and character features against the least-C class gives adjusted MI 0.24; the clusters are residue classes, with no structure beyond the residues.

Share of solutions/primes certified by small C: 91.8% of primes ≡1(4) are certified with C<=2 and mean C_min ≈ 2 (fingerprint #183). The share of the count f(p) from small C was not separately computed.

Depth-first scan over x for the two-term feasibility of 4/p − 1/x, on 120 primes in (10^3, 3·10^4]: the first feasible x lies within 0.3% of p/4 (max excess 0.28% of p, median 7·10^-5·p). The search tree is effectively one level deep.

On the fixed search space of pairs (C,k), C,k ≤ 200 (candidate d = 4Ck−1), over 588 primes in (10^3, 10^5]: median solutions M = 14, classical S/M median 2857, Grover √(S/M) ≈ 53. A square-root saving on a polynomial search space is not an ES gain.

Divisor criterion A (∃ d | 4Cp+1, d ≡ −1 mod 4C) against the HSP-type criterion B (−1 in the subgroup generated by prime-factor residues), over 12180 pairs (p ≤ 10^4, C ≤ 20): A implies B always, but B holds in 3998 pairs against 1814 for A. The subgroup test over-counts 2.2×, so it is no HSP shortcut.

Lookup (web search): Fermat two-squares algorithms (Cornacchia, hopping) and Zagier's windmill proof are classical; no source places two-square finding or its windmill involution in PPA as a search-problem class. Nothing transfers to ES.
Restatement: termination of 'for C = 1, 2, …: test(p, C)' for every p is exactly ES, since the loop terminates iff a certificate exists, so a ranking-function analysis restates the conjecture.

The first step is a formal observation, checked by reasoning: d | 4Cp+1 is a congruence condition on p mod d, so for any finite menu the success set is a finite union of residue classes and is b-automatic in every base. Nothing beyond the finite-menu residue structure follows.

Not run. Walnut needs a Java install, a base-4 automaton encoding of the window predicates for 4^s+297 and 15·2^s+1, and an automaton check: more than 1 h of setup and coding. The families are already settled by windows, so the expected gain is small.
next: Encode the 4^s+297 window predicate as a Walnut automatic-sequence statement and check the automaton against the known base-4 digit strings.

summary: For 120 primes (10^6–10^9) and C ≤ 50, every prime is solved by a good divisor (d ≡ −1 mod 4C, d | 4Cp+1) composed only of primes ≤ 10^3, but the smallest good divisor scales like N^{0.27–0.29} (median log10 d_min / log10 N = 0.29 and 0.26 in the two decades). A fixed trial-division bound therefore stops working as p grows, and at p ~ 10^100 the needed factors are of size ~p^0.28, far beyond ECM.
next: Measure the exponent of the minimal good divisor at p ~ 10^12–10^15 (full factorisation feasible) and check whether it stays near 0.28.

summary: Graffiti-lite over the features U, R+1, C_min, log p, log² p on 1600 primes ≡ 1 (mod 4), 1000 < p ≤ 3·10^4: the tightest simple ratios are log²p/log p (4.6–10.3), U/log²p ≥ 0.147 (minimum at p = 2521) and log p/C_min ≥ 0.03. No new inequality beyond the known size laws.
Gradient-boosted residue classifiers for (★) failure/R(p) and feature importances were covered by the fingerprint classical and character lanes (classical_corr.txt, fingerprint #152).
MLP on the last six decimal digits of p (one-hot) for the least-C class: 0.62 CV accuracy, below the 0.73 majority baseline. No digit signal.

Permutation importance of the gradient-boosted model: the top features are p mod 3, p mod 7, p mod 11, p mod 5 and (41/p), i.e. the model learns the known small-modulus structure; nothing beyond Z1384.

Not run. Stating 'ES holds for all 15·2^s+1' in Lean and running an LLM/ATP prover on it needs a prover setup and per-case runs (more than 1 h). The families are already settled by windows, so the value is as a prover benchmark.
next: Write the Lean statement for 15·2^s+1 with the window certificate as a hint and run one prover on the first 5 cases.

The sieve picture (which residues mod m are uncovered by the Type I/II families) is the dividing lane's CRT-avoidance computation (BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md: δ(X) ~ exp(−0.028 (ln X)^3)).
The finite-level projections K ∩ (Z/M) are the residue CRT-avoidance sets of the dividing lane (BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md, #0310–0313): δ(X) decays like exp(-c log³X).

Lookup (web search): the Bloom/Mehta unit-fractions Lean formalisation and the Xena formalisation of Erdős problems exist; they provide no ES lemma library, and ES is Erdős Problem #242 (OPEN). No partnership contact is made here.

Same computation as Z1778: all 120 sampled primes (10^6–10^9) have good divisors composed only of primes ≤ 10^3 for some C ≤ 50, but the minimal good divisor is ~N^0.28. The factoring-free question depends on that exponent at larger p (see Z1778).

Decidability questions for (ℕ,+,|) and divisibility-logic fragments are in the logic lanes (BRAINSTORM/z31_logic_divisibility.md, logic_divisibility_lgp.md).
Kolmogorov complexity is not computable. The item's own factorisations give residues mod 840 of 105, 441, 625, 105, 249, 385: two of six are squares (21², 25²). Nothing beyond this proxy.

A depth-6 decision tree on the (q/p) features (q ≤ 50) for C_min ≥ 2 reaches 0.709 CV accuracy, below the 0.731 majority baseline; gradient boosting on all residues reaches 0.817 (Z1384). Character features alone give no interpretable tree that beats the baseline.
Restatement: for fixed (t,u), v = (p+u)/(tu−1) is linear in p, so the fixed-letter slice is trivially a congruence condition; the uniform-in-p automaton impossibility is the item's own claim.
Restatement: an ultraproduct of failing primes is a nonstandard prime, and Łoś transfers the internal statements; the item gives no internal contradiction to test.

summary: Timing of the linear C-scan (C ≤ 50, full factorisation) on 10 random primes near each of 10^12, 10^14, 10^16: 0.3–0.6 ms per prime, with average C tried 2.1, 1.3, 1.2. The cost is dominated by the smallest C, with no visible growth in log p at this range.

Configuration-to-certificate lemmas are the window technique (FORCED_WINDOW.md) and the CRT-forced certificate checks of the dividing lane; the proposed automatic generator is an engineering version of these.

Checked by exact enumeration (scripts/z52b_p1_U08_corr.py): every prime p≡1(4) ≤ 3000 has an all-squarefree solution; 71 and 191 (≡3 mod 4) and 21169 (≡1 mod 4) have none (21169: 37 solutions, none squarefree). This confirms the item's exception list.
Meta/organisational: defining a hall-of-fame test set is bookkeeping, with no mathematical claim.
Restatement: symmetric functions with 4s3 = p·s2 rewrite the equation (e2/e3 = 4/n); the root search is the solution search.
Restatement: the CRT least positive representative is definitional, and the item gives no cost function beyond that representative.

Beatty-restricted search: 4/p = 1/x+1/y+1/z with x, y, z ∈ {⌊kα⌋} for α ∈ {√2, √3, √5, φ, √7} over 147 primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4) ≤ 2000: solvable for only 7–14 primes. Beatty denominators are too sparse for the equation.
LP: maximal zero mass consistent with the first three empirical moments of U (support 0..235): 0.092. The moments alone do not exclude sizeable P(U = 0), so the bound is weak.
Minimal unsatisfiable residue constraints are the dividing lane's CRT-avoidance sets (BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md), where the failing families are identified.

Entropy of divisor residues mod 840 for N with k prime factors: 0.693, 1.386, 2.038, 2.692, 3.317 nats for k = 1..5, which is exactly k·log 2. Divisor residues never collide, so elimination of small factors loses no entropy.
Restatement: tuv − u − v = p (and 4s3 = p·s2) is the definition of the parameter relation; there is no sparse relation beyond it to interpolate.
Meta/organisational: an active-learning sampling policy with no ES target statement.
Stratum hold-out: train on p ≡ 1 (mod 8), test on p ≡ 5 (mod 8) for the least-C class: accuracy 0.801 against a 0.722 majority baseline. The residue signal transfers across the mod-8 strata.

Primitive solutions: the repo already lists the primes ≤10^5 with no primitive solution (13, 37, 97, 181, 193, 277, 373, …; ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO Z0866). My check reproduces the listed primes 13, 37, 97, 181, 193, 277, 373, 541, 673, 757, 853, 1033, 1093, 1297, 1621 (20 such primes ≤ 3000 in total) (scripts/z52b_p1_U08_enum.py).
Under-specified: the item names no chart, parametrisation or variety, so no bad-reduction locus can be computed. This is neither a restatement nor a meta item, and it needs the chart named.

Algebra check: for p in a fixed piece ⌊p/m⌋ = q, r = qm − p changes by 1 per unit step of p, so the claimed AP with difference q holds only along a progression p ≡ const (mod q). The three-distance input does not apply as stated; no further test run.
Not run. A flag-algebra/LP bound for residue-menu coverage mod 840 needs the menu LP and dual certificates; more than 1 h of coding.

summary: Square-avoidance check for N_e = (p+e)/4 (e ≡ 3 mod 4 prime ≤ 199, p ≤ 2·10^4): 48.4% of the distinct prime factors of N_e are QR mod e (65211 factors, −8σ under an i.i.d. null); restricted to q > 100, 47.2% (12291 factors, −6.2σ). The windows for one p overlap across e, so the effective sample is smaller, and the bias is weak.
next: Repeat with one e per p (a random e per p) and a control of prime factors of random integers in the same range.

summary: Subset-product test: the fraction of random k-sets of residues mod e with a nonempty subset product ≡ −1 is 0.20–1.00 for e = 7 (k = 1..7) and 0.12–1.00 for e = 11. Forcing by subset products is generic; no polynomial structure (the Chevalley–Warning hypothesis) is supplied by the item.

Continued-fraction/resistor interpretations are in BRAINSTORM/z52b_translate.md (#6, #30–31).
Brute force over denominators dividing 60 (the 60-slot cycle): none of the 20 primes 7 ≤ p ≤ 200 with p ≡ 1 (mod 4) has 4/p = 1/a+1/b+1/c with a, b, c | 60.

The partition polynomial Σ_C S_C(p) t^C is the level-success table already tabulated (Z1128): its coefficients are 0/1 and its roots have median modulus 1.0003, with 40% within 0.02 of the unit circle. Nothing beyond the table.

summary: Lookup (web search): Marklof's Berry–Tabor results concern values of ternary forms at integers. The e-slice set is a sum over divisor pairs, not the value set of a binary form, so the analogy has no test.

Lookup (web search): 'Casimir energy Egyptian fraction' returns standard Casimir and zeta-regularisation literature; no unit-fraction identity emerges.
Restatement: with positive weights, Z_p(s) > 0 ⇔ some (C, d) exists, by definition; the 'identity' sought is the count itself.
Restatement: 1/μ = Σ 1/m_i for three integer masses is the equation 4/n = Σ 1/x_i rewritten; no physics content.
The Shor/HSP framing reduces to factoring 4Cp+1, which is Z2545 (small-factor sufficiency at 10^6–10^9; minimal good divisor ~N^0.28).
Not run. A QUBO encoding of the bit-blasted equation with exact diagonalisation for p ≤ 200 needs a multiplication-gadget encoder and an eigen-solver: more than 1 h of coding.

summary: The Dirichlet-character expansion #{a|N : a ≡ -1 (4C)} = (1/φ) Σ_χ χ(-1) Π(1+χ(q)+…) is the standard orthogonality identity (PROVED). It adds no new structure; the 'Ising chain' reading is a relabelling.
Restatement: Z(β) = Σ e^{−βE} with E = 0 exactly on certificates; the β → ∞ limit counts zero-energy trials by definition.

Oganesyan–Huse ratio of consecutive level spacings of log(4uC−1) over the successful (u, C), u, C ≤ 20, primes 1000–6000: mean r = 0.466 from 717 ratios, between Poisson (0.386) and GOE (0.531). The sample is small (a few levels per prime), so no spectral claim.

Box test (u, B ≤ 6, character modulus 10007): the actual weighted sum is −2.43, and the maximum over all ±1 sign patterns is 3.68 (ratio 1.5). The sign freedom changes the value by about 1.5× in this box; no magnetisation claim follows.

Annealed-vs-quenched gap log E[U] − E[log U] on dyadic ranges of primes p≡1(4) ≤ 3·10^4 (U = #solutions): 0.078, 0.066, 0.064, 0.056, 0.051, decreasing and consistent with σ²/2 of the lognormal fit (σ_log U ≈ 0.33–0.42). No disorder-specific effect.
Lookup (web search): 'Egyptian fractions and the ancient science of harmonics' is historical musicology; no link to 4/p or to certificate structure.
Lookup (web search): superparticular and epimoric-ratio literature concerns interval decompositions, not 4/p = Σ 1/x; no ES content transfers.
Restatement: Sylvester-wave and degeneracy formulas for the 2D oscillator are classical; 'p is a jump level' restates the counting function N(n; u, B).
Effective resistance A/p of the fan/ladder network is in BRAINSTORM/z52b_translate.md (#6, #117 family).

Legendre configuration on F_p (p ≡ 1 mod 4, p ≤ 2000, 147 primes): the bichromatic edge fraction over (x, x+1) is 0.503, and the longest monochromatic arc averages 0.024·p (max 0.40·p). No frustration signal beyond the random expectation.
Lookup (web search): Kleban–Özlük 'The Farey fraction spin chain' exists; no source identifies ES words with its states, and no computation was attempted.
Lookup (web search): Knauf's number-theoretical spin chain is established (Riemann zeroes, phase transitions); the by-excess analogue with a quadratic character is not in the sources found.
g(n) = Σ_sol 1/(xyz) over the solutions of 4/n, n ≤ 300: 0 of 412 coprime pairs (m, n ≤ 40, mn ≤ 300) satisfy g(mn) = g(m)g(n). The sum is not multiplicative, so no Euler product.
Restatement: the Gauss–Milgram sum of the 1×1 K-matrix is the classical quadratic Gauss sum; the 'ES sign' is the Legendre symbol already in the square-class lane.
Three-resistor topologies for r = n/4, 2 ≤ n ≤ 300: the parallel (ES) form realises all 299 values, and no n is realisable only by a series–parallel topology (B or C), so nothing new.

Lookup (web search): Beurling generalised primes/integers literature (Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer) studies prime counting, not an additive Beurling system in which ES fails; no construction found.

Exact check (scripts/z52b_p1_U08_enum.py rep): for primes p ≤ 1500, a/p has a 3-term unit-fraction representation for every p for a = 2..7 (238/238), and for a=8..12 in 94.5–99.2% of primes (failures are mostly small p). Small numerators are representable almost always, so the (log p)^4/p heuristic and the claim that '4 is special' are not supported.

summary: Random thinning of denominators (Monte Carlo, scripts/z52b_p1_U08_stats.py, 131 primes 1000<p≤3000): observed failure fraction 0.028 vs Poisson exp(−ρ³U) 0.014 at ρ=0.5, 0.37 vs 0.30 at ρ=0.3, 0.72 vs 0.69 at ρ=0.2. The Poisson prediction under-counts failures because 19% of solution pairs share a denominator (Z1130).
Selberg–Delange/Landau counts for H-confined integers are the Dirichlet-density lane (BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md, Selberg–Delange entries).
The Poisson PW model's m-dependence and the residue-model exception tests at m = 8..15 are in BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md (around l.65); the m=4 extrapolation is the open part.
The CRT avoidance density δ(X) ~ exp(−0.028 (ln X)³) over X = 56..1778 is already in BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md (l.38); the proposed extension to X=10^4 is the open part.
The comparison of observed δ(X) with the independent product is in BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md (independence prediction at X = 1000, l.44–60).
The m-family residue model at m = 8..15 with PW-table comparison is in BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md (l.65 onward); m=5..7 is the remainder.

Exact enumeration (scripts/z52b_p1_U08_enum.py nxworld, 211 primes p≡1(4) ≤ 3000): nx(p) ≈ U(p)/2.05 (median ratio), so nx tracks U rather than log p; the first-step expectation nx ≍ log p is not what the data show (corr with log p 0.74, with log²p 0.76).

The log-residual of U(p) against log log p (1531 primes p≡1(4), 1000<p≤30000) is clearly non-normal: skew −0.89, excess kurtosis 1.48. The lower tail is heavier than a normal fit: P(U≤20) = 0.52% observed vs 0.10% normal-predicted; the min is U=9 at p=2521. This matters for finite-exception heuristics that assume a light lower tail.
next: Refit the residual after removing the character features (fingerprint model) and check whether the skew and the 5× lower-tail excess persist.

summary: Composite U(pq) regression log U(pq) ≈ 3.0 + 0.20 log U(p) + 0.11 log U(q) + 0.26 log n over 5668 semiprimes is fingerprint item #162 (same numbers).
Vmin(p) ≤ 116 for all primes p≡1(4) ≤ 3·10^6 with records 3, 4, 7, 8, 23, 87, 116 is fingerprint #178–179; the extension to 10^9 is the open part.

Window minima of log(U/log³p) over 15 windows of 100 consecutive primes: mean window minimum −3.41 vs a crude Gumbel prediction −3.25 (median −2.26, sd 0.33); global minimum at 2521 (−3.98). The envelope is consistent with the lognormal-tail picture within 0.2 in log, no extra structure.

Pairwise correlations of level-C success events S_C(p) (C, D ≤ 40; 4772 primes ≡ 1 mod 4 up to 10^5): |corr| ≤ 0.175 (C=4, D=19), with a median joint-failure ratio of 1.000. The one notable pair is (C=1, C=2): P(both fail)/product = 0.69 globally, but 0.91 within mod-24 classes, so it is mostly a residue-class effect (Z2756).
Entropy of divisor residues mod 840 as the number of prime factors grows: exactly k·log 2 for k = 1..5 (no collisions among divisor residues).
Prime strata by small character values are the stratified residual analysis of H00 (Z0199: per-residue indicators) and the character-weight lane of the fingerprint (#152).
Pairing parity identity: for N = 4Cp+1, #{d | N : d ≡ −1 mod 4C} has the parity predicted by the d ↔ N/d pairing (N a square with √N ≡ −1). 0 mismatches over 8440 (p, C) pairs.

VC-type shattering by the Type I families (a, d, f; ad ≤ 60; 643 families) on a sample of 40 primes: some pair and some triple of primes are shattered, so the VC dimension is at least 3 at this sample size.
Spin enumeration (subset products of prime-power factors) equals divisor enumeration: identical for all 4 test N.
Roots of G_p(t) = Σ_{C ≤ 40} S_C(p) t^C over 5847 roots: median modulus 1.0003, 40% within 0.02 of the unit circle. Generic for 0/1 polynomials; no witness-set correlation was tested.
Overlap of solution pairs for 4/p (primes p≡1(4) ≤ 3000, 195183 pairs): 19.1% of pairs share at least one denominator; none share two. Solutions are mostly disjoint in denominators.

Finite-size scaling of R/log²p over decades: 0.179 (1000–3000), 0.157 (3000–10^4), 0.144 (10^4–3·10^4). A log-log fit on p ≤ 10^4 predicts mean R 12.7 at the upper decade, against 14.0 observed (9% miss): scaling is approximate, not a sharp collapse.
Density of states over (u, C) with u, C ≤ 20 and p ≡ 1 (mod 4) in (10^3, 3·10^3): gcd(p+u, 4uC−1) = 1 for 79.7% of the 52400 triples; the defect distribution is 3 (9.9%), 5 (3.1%), 7 (1.8%).

Family-prime incidence (40 primes, Type I families with ad ≤ 60): top singular value 9.05 against 8.75 ± 0.13 under a checkerboard-swap null that preserves row and column sums, i.e. 2.4σ on this sample. Not significant enough to claim structure.
Meta/organisational: software practice (randomised identity testing) with no ES claim attached.

For 120 sampled primes (10^6–10^9) and C ≤ 50: 80% and 75% of the prime factors q of 4Cp+1 have q−1 1000-smooth in the two decades. Pollard-type p−1 steering would find most factors of these N, but the item gives no mechanism linking that to ES.
Las Vegas sampling of C uniform on 1..200 has success rate 0.025 per trial (expected 40 trials at the median), against a linear scan with median C_min = 1. Scan order is already optimal here.
Schedule test: the first-success index for a fixed random permutation of C has median 23 (p90 67), against median 1 (p90 2) for the linear scan. Small-bias or randomised schedules do not help.
Meta/organisational: property-based testing practice with no ES claim attached.

Two-point structure of U along primes: lag-1,2,3 autocorrelation of the log-residual is −0.120, −0.047, −0.006 (1600 primes p≡1(4), 100<p≤30000; see Z1746). No RMT-type level repulsion test was run beyond this; the lag-1 value is the only significant feature.

C_min(p) distribution (the first-step computation) is in fingerprint #180 and #183 (C_min = 1 for 76.6%, ≤2 for 91.8%, records to 23105). The percolation graph on C is not computed, but adds nothing beyond the C_min histogram.
S(p)=log U(p) tails: the log-residual is left-skewed (skew −0.89) and not Gaussian (see Z0809); the Erdős–Kac-type normal law for ω(4Cp+1) is not the right comparison here. Nothing beyond Z0809.

Moments of U over dyadic ranges (p≡1(4), 100<p≤30000): log-log slopes of ⟨U^q⟩ vs log p are −0.82 (q=−2), −0.37 (q=−1), 0.35 (q=1), 0.70 (q=2), 1.04 (q=3), 1.38 (q=4): the moments grow smoothly, with no sign of intermittency beyond the lognormal shape.

Type I and Type II counts (definitions as in the Z0650 text) on 1600 primes: P(f_I = 0) = 0.0006, P(f_II = 0) = 0.013, P(both = 0) = 0.0006, mutual information 0.0027 nats. Type I families almost always hit, so the zero indicators are essentially constant.

Pairwise correlations of level-C success events over 4772 primes ≤ 10^5 (Z1042): joint-failure ratio median 1.000 over pairs. Triples of C ≡ 1 (mod 4) give median ratio 0.998 (range 0.85–1.07, Z1525); the (1,2) pair is the exception and is mostly class-explained.
Choosing C with small φ(4C) is the small-C structure already in the C_min data: C = 1, 2 certify 92% of primes (fingerprint #183).
Independence across triples of C ≡ 1 (mod 4) on 4772 primes: joint-failure ratio to the product has median 0.998 (range 0.85–1.07 over 120 triples). Independence holds for these parameter triples.

R(p) = Σ_{C ≤ 200} #good divisors on 1600 primes (1000 < p ≤ 3·10^4): mean 12.9, variance 32.6 (dispersion 2.5, so not Poisson), negative-binomial dispersion k ≈ 8.4, zero fraction 0.3%, and skew −1.05 of log(1+R). The shape is the left-skewed log law seen for U (Z0809), not a Poisson or REM-type count.
Cramér-type expected-counterexample sums Σ_p exp(−c log²p) are the lottery model (BRAINSTORM/prob_lottery_model.md) and the zero-law of the campaign.
Variance of R(p) − M_BM(p) in windows and the BM main-term data are in BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md / scripts/z52b_fingerprint_bm.py and H00 Z0042 (bmweights.json).

Mutual information between the least-C class and p mod 840: 0.64 bits against a 0.17-bit shuffle null (plug-in bias with 192 classes); with p mod 8 it is 0.0003 against 0.0018. Any excess sits in the residues mod 3, 5, 7, not in mod 8.
Random CSP thresholds for k-term ES-type systems are the random-integer lottery model; BRAINSTORM/prob_lottery_model.md treats the random analogues.

Lag autocorrelation of log R residuals: within mod-840 classes lag 1 = 0.31 and lag 2 = 0.30, which is a class-mean effect because the residuals are not demeaned per class; over all primes lag 1 = −0.03.

Clumping test on the level-success table (1600 primes): P(no success for C ≤ K) observed 0.036 at K = 5, against 0.059 for the independent product and 0.140 for Poisson clumping; at K = 40, 0.005 against 0.008 and 0.021. The independent product is nearer than Poisson, and the observed value is about 0.6 of it.
Greedy template cover of the 1600 primes ≡ 1 (mod 4) up to 3·10^4 (C ≤ 200; 1595 covered): 15 templates reach 90%, 70 reach 99%, 84 reach 99.9%. The top template covers 813 primes.
Scribal/Rhind-type rules and greedy/small-denominator heuristics are classified in BRAINSTORM/greedy_algorithm_dynamics.md and the Egyptian-fraction algorithm survey of the z52b lanes.
The alteration step cannot change N, as the item says. The level success rates on the same table are P_C = 0.73, 0.45, 0.30, 0.28, 0.20 for C = 1..5, so nothing beyond the table.
Shape of the 6256 solutions of 4/p, primes 1000 ≤ p ≤ 3000 (p ≡ 1 mod 4): mean log x/log p = 0.83, mean log y/log p = 1.39, mean log z/log p = 2.28, corr(log y, log z) = 0.20.

Existence against expected count μ_K = mean R_{≤K} on 600 primes: P(R_{≤K} = 0) observed 0.043 at K = 5 (μ = 6.0) against Poisson 0.0025, and 0.0067 against 10^-4 at K = 50 (μ = 9.6). Poisson under-predicts empty-existence events badly, since R is overdispersed across levels.

Maier-type QR-class test at p ≈ 10^12: primes ≡ 1 (mod 840) that are QR modulo every prime 11..47 have mean R_{≤60}/log²p = 0.032 (n = 120) against 0.044 for random primes of the same size, a 26% deficit at ~4σ. This matches the character-weight effects in the fingerprint lane (#152).
Lookup (web search): the erdosproblems.com #314 text was not retrieved, so the ES F-item mapping cannot be checked here. Inconclusive; nothing tested.
Random covering and coupon-collector heuristics for residue families are the CRT-avoidance lane (BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md: δ(X) and independence comparison).
Poisson heuristics for representation counts are the lottery model (BRAINSTORM/prob_lottery_model.md) and the Poisson comparisons of the dividing lane.
Lower-tail large deviations for representation counts are the LOWER_TAIL_* / LDP_DEEP lanes (LOWER_TAIL_FABLE.md, LDP_DEEP.md).
Not run. The involution graph on solutions is not defined in the item. Defining the Vieta-type moves (see INVOLUTION_ES.md) and computing first-return probabilities is more than 1 h of coding.

Fractional lower-tail moments of U (p≡1(4), 1000<p≤30000): E[U^{-0.5}] = 0.117, E[U^{-1}] = 0.0148, E[U^{-2}] = 3.3·10^{-4}. Finite and decaying; nothing singular in the lower tail.
OAI 142 (deterministic factoring over F_p) is assessed in OAI_METHOD_142.md; ES search uses square roots mod p only through the deterministic path already discussed there.

PARI/GP via cypari2: isprime(2054098191162848070241) returns 1. PARI's default isprime is a proof (not a probable-prime test), so the hardest repo prime is rigorously prime. No certificate file was written.

Block-minimum change-point check on U/log³p: the window-minimum analysis (Z0883) shows no regime shift; global minimum at 2521 is the known one, and the block means decrease smoothly with log p (Jensen gaps 0.078→0.051, Z1759).
Parity layers of R(p)/2 mod 2 and the local-symbol predictors are in the parity audit lanes (PARITY_AUDIT.md, PARITY_FIXED_P.md).
Not run. A Kubilius/PD-model simulation of R(p) with exact local factors at 2, 3, 5, 7 and a lower-tail comparison needs a model implementation: more than 1 h.

summary: BDH-type class-variance ratios Σ_a (Σ_{p≡a}(U−Ū))² / Σ(U−Ū)² on 1600 primes: 127 (mod 8), 92 (mod 24), 40 (mod 12), 20 (mod 5), 6 (mod 7), 1.3 (mod 13). The ratios are driven by class-mean differences of U, which are the character effects in the fingerprint lane (#152).
Selberg–Delange-type asymptotics for class-restricted divisor generating functions are the Selberg–Delange lane in BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md.

Gowers/Nikolov–Pyber size check for SL₂(F_p): |A||B||C| ≈ p³ against |G|³/m ≈ p⁸ (deficit ≈ p⁵). The reduction mod q is far from the Gowers threshold; the same arithmetic appears in H05 (Z1915, Gowers–Green–Manners–Tao lane).

Lookup (web search): Chatterjee's 'Nonlinear large deviations' (arXiv 1401.3495) and the gradient-complexity line apply to low-complexity functions; the item's hypothesis (R(p) has low gradient complexity) is not verified, so no conclusion is drawn.

SPRT-type likelihood ratio, hard (C_min ≥ 3) vs easy (C_min ≤ 2) primes: after K failed levels the ratio is about 9–11 for K = 2, 5, 10 (58–163 primes failing), with per-level rates 0.00 and 0.00 for hard primes at C = 1, 2. The statistic is informative but gives no ES consequence.
Lookup (web search): 2026 Legendre-PRF cryptanalysis papers concern keyed symbols; the item notes that (·/p) is public, so the PRF hypothesis does not apply, and nothing is tested.

Extinction and branching check on the level table (1600 primes): P(no success for C ≤ 5) observed 0.036, product 0.059. Pair ratio for (C=1, C=2) is 0.69 globally but 0.91 within mod-24 classes, and the K = 5 all-fail ratio stays at about 0.74 within mod-24 classes (~2σ). No tree-like structure is established.
Lookup (web search): Katz–Sarnak and monodromy literature (the 'Katz–Sarnak philosophy'). No monodromy group for the divisor-in-class counting sheaf is identified in the sources found.

4/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z² (one square denominator): all 87 primes p≡3(4) ≤ 1000 are solvable (first z ≤ 474), but 37 of 80 primes p≡1(4) ≤ 1000 have no solution with z ≤ 600 (brute force), and the 20 checked persist to z ≤ 4000 (17, 29, 41, 73, 89, 101, 109, 149, 173, 197, 241, 269, 277, 281, 421, …). Solvable p≡1(4) have first z ≤ 26 (median 12); no small residue or Legendre pattern explains the split (see md).
next: Test a Hilbert-symbol / Brauer–Manin obstruction for the conic bundle 4xyz²=n(xz²+yz²+xy) at the failing primes (e.g. 17, 29, 41), and check whether any failing p has a solution with z > 4000.

Exhaustive check (scripts/z52b_p1_U08_enum.py nxworld): for the 211 primes p≡1(4), 5≤p≤3000, no solution of 4/p has all three denominators in {p} ∪ primes ∪ 2·primes, except p=5 (2+5+10). Also no solution with all denominators prime at any such p. The prime-type world is essentially empty in this range, stronger than the 'x prime' figure in the item.
Over F_q (q prime ≤ 200), 4/n = Σ 1/x_i with nonzero-square x_i fails only for q = 3 (residues 1,2 not in S+S+S with S = {1}). No failure for any q ≥ 5 up to 200.
